title: How do we complete a figure around a blue line?
description: Five red outlines on squared paper sit beside blue lines, some straight and some slanted. Each outline is completed by marking matching points on the other side of the blue line.
teaching_notes: One idea: count each corner's distance from the blue line and mark the matching corner the same distance on the other side. Watch for students who copy the shape by sliding it instead of flipping it, and for students who skip turning the page for slanted lines.

source: Copy the following on squared paper. Complete them so that the blue line is a line of symmetry. Problem (a) has been done for you. Hint: for (c) and (f), see if rotating the book helps!
video_script.why: The child completes red outlines around a blue line by marking each matching corner at the same distance on the other side.
video_script.substitution: Count each corner's distance from the blue line, mark the matching corner at the same distance on the other side, and join the matching corners.
video_script.anchor: Five red outlines on squared paper beside blue lines: a stepped shape above a horizontal line, a staircase beside a slanted line, a small shape on a vertical line, a five sided shape below a horizontal line, and a cut corner shape beside a slanted line
video_script.payoff_line: Mark each matching point at the same distance on the other side.

final_answer.value: mirror every point of the red outline in the blue line, then join the matching points
final_answer.spoken: mirror every point of the red outline in the blue line, then join the matching points

never_show: the finished shapes before the answer beat
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
Each matching point is at the same distance from the line as the original point, on the other side.
The stepped shape above the horizontal line is mirrored below it, and the five sided shape below its horizontal line is mirrored above it.
The small shape on the vertical line has its left red part mirrored to the right.
For a slanted blue line, turn the page so that the line is vertical or horizontal, then mirror as usual.
Check: the red part and the new part cover each other exactly when folded on the blue line.
video_script.design: One idea: count the distance, then go the same distance on the other side. Assumes the child has seen corners cross a line of symmetry. The five outlines stay on the board from the hook to the end.
open_questions: The five outlines are described in words by the worklist and could not be seen, so each is treated as a corner by corner mirror drawing around its blue line.
